nodes.label: Git Commit Convention
nodes.rationale: Commit small and one logical change per commit so each verified step is independently revertible; a claim of success only counts if the tests, build, or program were actually run, because an unverified claim is a guess. Stage only changed files (never 'git add -A') to avoid sweeping up the human's in-progress work. Commit format '<type>(<scope>): <summary>' with type in feat/fix/chore/docs/refactor/test/perf and a concrete scope keeps history searchable and matches existing repo history.

nodes.label: Graphify Sync Policy
nodes.rationale: The graph in graphify-out/ is committed like source, but is regenerated once per verified batch rather than per commit, and only when stale relative to graphify-out/manifest.json. This avoids graph churn in every commit while keeping the architecture graph trustworthy; it never blocks an answer because it is reported in one line of the summary.

nodes.label: Authoritative Database Functions and Triggers
nodes.rationale: These routines must stay authoritative rather than being reimplemented in TypeScript: registration_b4transaction() enforces prerequisite, duplicate, and lock checks; create_assessment()/delete_assessment() own fee computation; compute_gpa()/compute_gpa_all() own GPA; get_payment_schedule_spc()/get_partial_assessment_spc() and get_next_orno() own schedule and OR-number allocation; semstudent_b4transaction(), semstudent_stamp(), and collection_header_get_orno() own enrolment and collection invariants.

nodes.label: electron/main.cjs and electron/live.cjs Bridge
nodes.rationale: The bridge reads srgb.ini from the executable folder, resources, the SERMS parent folder, or the working directory; opens a pg client with a 7-second timeout; verifies current_user, current_database(), and server version; and performs a read-only check against srgb.semester, srgb.student, and srgb.semstudent. It never stores the password in the renderer or on disk.

nodes.label: Rave Reports Print Layouts
nodes.rationale: The old forms are Rave Reports 5 .rav files in the SERMS root; printable COR, assessment, OR, TOR, and CHED forms should be reproduced from the same data. Phase 0 intentionally does not print.

nodes.label: srgb.registration Grade Write
nodes.rationale: Grade entry is not a separate upload service: the old grade-sheet dataset updates srgb.registration directly, keyed on sy, sem, studid, subjcode. Because it is a direct database write rather than a file upload, the feature only works on the school network.

nodes.label: srgb.ini Configuration
nodes.rationale: The original reads srgb.ini next to the executable or working folder for pghostname, pgport, pgdbname, and photohost, then connects to PostgreSQL through libpq/ADO.

nodes.label: Phase Scope: Working UI Prototype on Synthetic Data
nodes.norm_label: phase scope: working ui prototype on synthetic data
nodes.rationale: Delivered scope is a working UI prototype with synthetic data, desktop shell, responsive layouts, payment flow, grade sheet, command palette, and a real PostgreSQL connection test. Explicitly out of scope for now: full 146-form parity, live read/write queries for every module, exact legacy print layouts, and migration tooling.

nodes.label: SERMS Modern
nodes.rationale: A replacement interface for St. Peter's College's Student Enrolment and Records Management System, aimed at the staff who run the Registrar, Cashier, Accounting, Faculty, and Administration desks every day.

nodes.label: Desk Roles: Registrar, Cashier, Accounting, Faculty, Administrator
nodes.norm_label: desk roles: registrar, cashier, accounting, faculty, administrator
nodes.rationale: The primary device is a Windows office PC on the school network, designed for a desk with a keyboard; tablet and phone remain usable for quick lookups only.

nodes.label: Electron Desktop Shell and Build Pipeline
nodes.norm_label: electron desktop shell and build pipeline
nodes.rationale: The launcher uses the installed Electron runtime to load the bundled release/win-unpacked/resources/app.asar because the generated unsigned .exe may be blocked by Windows Application Control; the launcher is the reliable local path. SERMS Modern.lnk is machine-local and intentionally not committed.

nodes.label: Live PostgreSQL Bridge via srgb.ini
nodes.rationale: The original app talks directly to PostgreSQL at 192.168.8.10:5432/dbspc and has no separate grade-upload service: the grade sheet writes grade components to srgb.registration on the school server, which is why it only works on the school network. The prototype deliberately introduces no API server or new upload service, and keeps live writes confirmation-gated and read-only where financial records are concerned.

nodes.label: 146-Form Parity Gap
nodes.rationale: The original has 146 business forms, 15 role menus, 110 tables, and 205 database functions. The prototype covers the daily student/registration/cashier/academic loop but does not claim one-for-one parity with every administrative form or report; the remaining gap is tracked in docs/LIVE-DATA.md.

nodes.label: Live Data Risks
nodes.rationale: srgb.registration.prelim, midterm, and final exist alongside prelim1..4, so the old grade-sheet mapping must be confirmed before any write. Payment/OR allocation is transactional and audit-sensitive; report layouts are operationally important; the database is only reachable on the school network; the 2020 dump is old so the live schema may have changed; and student photos use an FTP store whose embedded credentials must not be carried forward.

nodes.label: Write Mapping: Grade, Payment, Assessment, COR
nodes.norm_label: write mapping: grade, payment, assessment, cor
nodes.rationale: Do not invent write flows; match the original transaction boundaries. Grade save updates the four prelim1..4 components and remarks and lets the database trigger compute the cumulative grade. Payment uses the same OR-number allocation and payment/collection_* inserts in one transaction. Assessment calls srgb.create_assessment()/srgb.delete_assessment() rather than computing fees in TypeScript. COR add/drop inserts/deletes srgb.registration and lets registration_b4transaction() enforce prerequisites, duplicates, and locks.

nodes.label: Product Principles
nodes.rationale: One student one workspace; show the next step; respect the existing rules (the PostgreSQL schema, triggers, and functions remain the source of truth); no invented upload (grades, assessments, and payments write directly to the school server as they do today); quiet confidence rather than generic SaaS decoration; print matters because the office still runs on official documents; no data risk in design work (prototype with synthetic records, validate live writes on a test copy).

nodes.label: One Student, One Workspace
nodes.rationale: The legacy SERMS is functionally rich but fragmented: staff move between fixed-size forms, menus, and modal lookups to complete one student transaction, and the student (the object everyone needs) is not the organising idea. SERMS Modern reorganises the work around the student record as a five-step loop: find the student, see the whole record, take the next action, print or post the result, leave an audit trail.

nodes.label: Visual Direction: Maroon and Gold, Newsreader and Inter
nodes.norm_label: visual direction: maroon and gold, newsreader and inter
nodes.rationale: Deep maroon and warm gold come from the school seal, on warm paper background with white work surfaces and ink text. Newsreader for display and Inter for UI and tables. 240 px sidebar, 66 px top bar, generous page rhythm, dense but readable tables. Motion is restricted to page enter, modal enter, and press feedback, with no animation on high-frequency actions.

nodes.label: Safety and Secret-Handling Notes
nodes.rationale: All visible demo records are synthetic and no production data is in the folder; srgb.ini credentials, student records, and the database dump must not be committed. The original binary contains a hard-coded FTP account for student photos which is deliberately not reused; photo upload moves to configuration before being wired. The unsigned Windows executable may be blocked by Application Control, so the launcher is used locally or the build must be signed.
